newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-OPSM sees 10 pct half-yr profit rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-OPSM sees 10 pct half-yr profit rise.

text.p: Protective equipment and eyewear maker OSPM Protector Ltd said on Friday that if present sales trends continued it expected its first half profit to be about 10 percent higher than the previous year's half.

"If present sales trends continue, we expect OSPM Protector's first half profit to be around 10 percent above that for the first half of last year," chairman Adrian Lane told shareholders at the company's annual meeting.
"The company's total sales for the first quarter of 1996/97 were ahead of those for the first quarter of last year, but below our expectations," Lane said.

Lane said the shortfall against budget was caused partly by subdued retail demand in Australia, particularly in New South Wales. Also, there was slower economic actvity in New Zealand, due in part to the election and high interest rates.

"I am, however, pleased to advise shareholders that the internal changes, particularly in the OPSM and Protector Technologies groups, have enabled us to achieve a first quarter profit ahead of that for the first quarter if last year," he said.

OPSM reported a net profit of A$11.12 million in the six months ended December 31 1995, marginally down on the previous year. It posted a net profit of A$22.13 million for the year to June 30, 1996, compared with A$24.46 milllion in 1994/95.
At 11.55 a.m. (0055 GMT), OSPM shares were six cents up at A$2.80. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
